issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s right to purchase land is not extinguished by a pending ejectment proceeding or defeated by a later ejectment order if the tenant was still a tenant when the purchase right was exercised.
material_facts: The tenant had continuously occupied the land for the minimum period required to claim the statutory purchase right.
The landowner had begun an ejectment proceeding alleging non-payment of rent, but no ejectment order had been passed when the tenant applied to purchase the land.
The tenant’s purchase application was made before the ejectment order was passed.
issues.conclusion: The tenant was entitled to exercise the purchase right while the ejectment proceeding was pending, and the later ejectment order did not defeat that right.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 9, 14-A and 18 of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, a tenancy is determined only in the prescribed conditions and manner; instituting an ejectment proceeding does not itself terminate the tenancy. A tenant who has completed the continuous occupation period required by section 18 remains entitled to purchase while still a tenant, and a later ejectment order does not retrospectively defeat a purchase right already exercised. Har Sarup v. Financial Commissioner, Revenue, Punjab, (1965) 44 Lah. L.T. 157, was approved.

rule.if: purchase_claim_in_ejectment_case and six_year_continuous_occupation and tenant_status_at_purchase_claim and no_ejectment_order_at_purchase_claim

predicates.purchase_claim_in_ejectment_case: A tenant’s claim to purchase land is made while an ejectment proceeding concerning that tenancy is pending.
predicates.six_year_continuous_occupation: The tenant has continuously occupied the land for the minimum period required to claim the purchase right.
predicates.tenant_status_at_purchase_claim: The tenant remains a tenant when the purchase claim is made.
predicates.no_ejectment_order_at_purchase_claim: No order ejecting the tenant has been passed when the purchase claim is made.

issues.definition: When a qualifying tenant makes a purchase claim before an ejectment order is passed, a later ejectment order does not defeat the purchase right.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant exercising the right to purchase land must pay the determined compensation together with rent that remains due.
material_facts: A proceeding to recover rent from the tenant had been commenced.
The authority determined compensation payable for the purchase, but it was unclear whether that amount included the rent in arrears.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could purchase the land on payment of the determined compensation together with the rent due, with the authority to direct payment in appropriate instalments.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the Punjab Security of Land Tenures Act, 1953, provides for purchase on payment of determined compensation; under section 18(4)(a), payment may be directed in appropriate instalments. The Court required rent due to be paid in addition to compensation because it was unclear whether the determined amount already included the arrears.

predicates.tenant_purchase_claim: A tenant claims to purchase land under a statutory purchase right.
predicates.rent_arrears_remain_due: Rent owed by the tenant remains unpaid when the purchase claim is determined.

issues.definition: A tenant who claims to purchase land while rent remains unpaid must pay both the purchase compensation and the rent arrears.
